original.description: An Austro-Hungarian siege gun in Belgium, from a Bain News Service glass negative (5 × 7 in. or smaller). The Library of Congress title reads "Austrian siege gun in Belg. (i.e., Belgium)".
original.photographer: not named on the negative; published by Bain News Service
original.archive: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LCCN 2014698051, via Wikimedia Commons
original.licence: public domain (Commons record: LicenseShortName "Public domain"; Permission "Image from Library of Congress Prints and Photographs division"). The Bain collection carries no known restrictions; the record links the catalogue entry at https://lccn.loc.gov/2014698051.

colorization.status: not colorized. Recommendation: colorize — the highest-resolution item in the shot list and the siege-artillery card’s natural hero.

content_policy: ok — a gun and its crew, no gore
caption: An Austro-Hungarian siege gun in Belgium, 1914. Austria-Hungary lent Germany the Škoda 30.5 cm mortars that worked alongside Krupp’s 42 cm howitzers against the Belgian forts — the alliance’s most useful contribution in the west.
credit: Original photograph: Bain News Service, 1914; Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LCCN 2014698051; public domain.
notes: Verified 2026-08-24 against the Commons file record via the MediaWiki API. The archive title says "Austrian siege gun" and gives no model; the caption above names the Škoda 30.5 cm as the Austro-Hungarian type in Belgium in general terms rather than identifying the piece in frame. The image review (sand-y0u.7) should either confirm the model from the carriage or the caption should drop the number.
